column1: # What tells near-synonyms apart, where CC-CEDICT gives them the same gloss.
# Hand-written, and this project's own — not generated, and not CC-CEDICT's.
# Drafted by Claude (Anthropic) from general knowledge of Mandarin usage, for
# the words a learner actually meets: syllabus words that share a gloss and
# that the dictionary has no other way to separate.
# Cross-checked by Qwen 3.8-Max (Alibaba), a Chinese-first model, asked first
# to verify the file and then, twice, to name the least accurate notes. Its
# corrections to 吓/吓唬, 过滤/筛选, 犹豫/迟疑, 饭店/旅馆, 出丑, 土匪, 缴费,
# 腮, 延 and 有幸 were taken; 单身/独身, 不免/必将, 比如/例如 and 渐渐 were
# rewritten more moderately than it proposed; its claims about 括弧 and 书橱
# could not be confirmed and were not taken. Two models
# agreeing is not a native speaker, so this still wants review by one, or by a
# teacher; a correction is a one-line edit here.
# One word per line, four fields separated by tabs:
#   simplified   the word, exactly as CC-CEDICT writes it
#   key          its dictionary key, tone numbers and all
#   register     everyday, formal, or - where register is not the difference
#   note         what it is used for, in a few words. Pinyin, never characters:
#                this is on the learning surface.
# The test in test/translation/word_notes_test.dart checks every line points
# at a real dictionary entry, uses a known register, holds no characters, and
# that words sharing a gloss do not share a note.
